quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: What problems can worn or bald tires cause?

options.text: Can make turning more difficult.
Are likely to hydroplane.
Can increase your stopping distance.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance and make turning harder. Tires without good tread also increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention to the road
Driving too fast for road conditions
Following other vehicles too closely
All of the above

questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end collisions happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: Which substances can impair your driving and lead to a DUI arrest?

options.text: Beer, wine, and other alcohol
Illegal drugs or prescription medicines
Inhalants like glue or paint
All of the above

questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. These include alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medicines (prescription and over-the-counter).

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road intersects with a divided highway.
You are on an overpass above a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road intersects with a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that your road intersects with a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or guide rail.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires properly maintained.
Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Watch out for standing water or puddles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, your car needs more distance to stop and may skid on turns. Do not use cruise control in wet or icy conditions. Reduce speed and drive carefully.

questions.question: When should you slow down?

options.text: On narrow or winding roads.
At intersections or railroad crossings.
When the road is wet or slippery.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp curves, where there are pedestrians, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing warning sign?

options.text: Drive faster than the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is near.
Look for a way around lowered gates.
Assume no trains are near and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is near.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing signs warn drivers that a train may be coming. Always obey these signs and never go around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a last-minute turn at an exit. If you miss your exit, go to the next one.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop.
Fines double in a work zone.
Stop ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings and alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns of bicycles crossing the road.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, what must you do?

options.text: Always signal, even if no other cars are visible.
Signal only if other cars are visible.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if no other cars are visible.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from a curb. Do not skip signaling even when you think no one is watching.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving
All of the above

questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, you should:

options.text: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as he or she passes you.
Speed up as he or she passes you.
Block the passing lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: Get out of the aggressive driver's way. Do not look at them or make eye contact. Do not speed up or block them, as this will make them more angry and dangerous.

questions.question: When approaching a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
Honk your horn before passing the bus on its left.
Continue driving when you think most kids are done exiting the bus.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped school bus with its stop signal on, you must come to a complete stop. Do not proceed until the stop arm is withdrawn.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: A minor traffic safety problem.
A serious traffic safety problem.
Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
Only dangerous to the driver who drinks.

questions.explanation: Driving while impaired or intoxicated is a serious traffic safety problem. Safe driving is not possible after drinking alcohol or taking drugs. Impaired driving endangers you and everyone else on the road.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Yield.
Crossroad ahead.
Keep right.
Yield ahead.

questions.explanation: This triangular sign tells you to slow down when approaching an intersection and be ready to stop. Let other drivers and pedestrians go first. You may proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: Braking distance is affected by:

options.text: How fast your vehicle is traveling.
The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the pavement.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on your vehicle's speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road surface.

questions.question: Do not pass:

options.text: On a hill or curve.
When school bus lights are flashing.
When approaching an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Never pass on hills, curves, at intersections, at railroad crossings, on bridges, or in no passing zones. Do not pass a school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided highway.

questions.question: Distracted driving may be caused by:

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Drivers must make 200 decisions for every mile traveled. You must focus your full attention on driving. Any additional task is a dangerous distraction.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or at an equipment check, you must show:

options.text: Proof of insurance.
Your license.
Proof of registration.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must have your license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance in your vehicle when driving. You must show all three documents when stopped.

questions.question: An intersection has no traffic signs or signals. You arrive at the same time as a vehicle to your right. You should:

options.text: Speed up and go through the intersection.
Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk your horn and drive through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, when two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Wait until it passes safely before you proceed.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Do what other drivers are doing, even if the crossing guard says something different.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Be ready to slow down and drive carefully when a crossing guard tells you to. Always drive with extra caution in school zones.

questions.question: When approaching a curve in the road, you should reduce your speed:

options.text: Only if you want to.
Only if you feel unsafe.
Before you enter the curve.
After you are halfway through the curve.

questions.explanation: Always slow down before a curve or when you cannot see clearly ahead. Reduce your speed before entering the curve so you do not have to brake while turning. Braking in a curve can cause your car to skid.

questions.question: What colors are signs that show the distance to the next highway exit?

options.text: Yellow with black letters
Black with white letters
Red with white letters
Green with white letters

questions.explanation: Signs that give information about where to go are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle's signal. You should:

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are open for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as fast as you can.
Slow down, move to give the emergency vehicle a clear path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to give the emergency vehicle a clear path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights, slow down, clear a path for the emergency vehicle, and stop. Do not try to drive faster than the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: A sign of a drunk driver is:

options.text: Weaving between lanes.
Driving slower than other traffic.
Making quick and sudden stops.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving between lanes, driving slower than other traffic, jerking movements, and making quick and sudden stops.
